newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. makes appointment to retirement board.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. makes appointment to retirement board.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Monday appointed Yvonne Gallegos Bodle to the State Teachers' Retirement Board.

Bodle is a professor of business at Ventura Community College, a position she has held since 1965. A Republican, Bodle has served on the Community Colleges Board of Governors since 1991 and currently chairs the committees on economic development and vocational education.

The Teachers' Retirement Board is a 12-member panel that includes the state treasurer, controller, superintendent of public instruction, director of finance and eight members appointed by the governor to four year terms.
The board provides policy guidance and general direction for the California State Teachers' Retirement System, which is the largest teachers' pension plan in the United States.

The system has about 350,000 active members. An additional 130,000 people receive benefits from the system, which has more than $60 billion in assets dedicated to the payment of current and future benefits.
Board members do not receive a salary. The appointment does not require state Senate confirmation.
